text:
maria: hitting a weird error in py-sdk 0.7.3 (async client). server returns 422 text/plain 'Validation error: email missing' but SDK attempts json.loads and we end up with JSONDecodeError -> generic RedwoodAPIError with no http status or raw body attached. any ideas?

jamal: can you paste a minimal repro + the stacktrace? async call or sync?

maria: async. repro:
```py
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=...) as c:
    await c.users.create({'name': 'Alex'})  # server responds 422 text/plain
```
stack snippet:
```
File "/.../redwood/client.py", line 212, in _handle_response
  parsed = json.loads(body)  # raises JSONDecodeError
  ...
redwood.errors.RedwoodAPIError: failed to parse error body
```
HTTP response headers: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body: `Validation error: email missing`

maria: result is the exception has no `http_status` attr and `raw_body` is not preserved, so callers can't differentiate validation vs auth errors. sync client seems slightly better.

tessa: I think we intentionally added `raw_body` preservation in sync paths last quarter but missed the async exception path (error handling lives in a shared helper but async wrapper swallows extra attrs).

arjun: repro looks clear. proposal: when parsing error body fails, set error.parsed_body = None, error.raw_body = body (decoded text), and error.http_status = resp.status. Keep the original parse exception chained (cause) but preserve the HTTP metadata on the raised SDK error. Also update typing stub so RedwoodAPIError has `http_status: Optional[int]` and `raw_body: Optional[str]`.

kate: agreed. also add an ergonomic helper: `RedwoodAPIError.get_json()` that returns parsed json or raises a clear exception; and document the canonical pattern:
```py
try:
  await client.users.create(...)
except RedwoodAPIError as e:
  print('status', e.http_status)
  print('raw', e.raw_body)
  print('json', e.parsed_body)
```
This'll help teams that hit weird text/plain errors from proxies.

dev-bot: CI: py-sdk/async-error-preserve branch — build failed on lint (flake8: missing docstring) <https://ci.example/py-sdk/1234|details>

jamal: i'll pick up the PR. should this be 0.7.4 patch? it's a bugfix and should be small.

maria: yes patch level. must include async parity, tests for text/plain and html error bodies, and a mypy-friendly stub update.

arjun: tests: add unit that fakes an aiohttp response with content-type text/plain and ensures exception.http_status == 422 and exception.raw_body == 'Validation error: email missing'. also add a mypy check to CI job.

tessa: small note: watch out for binary bodies (images or gzipped errors). raw_body should be `Optional[bytes]` in impl but expose decoded `str` in the public attribute and preserve None if decoding fails. but for typing it's easier to keep `raw_body: Optional[str]` and add `raw_bytes: Optional[bytes]` if we need binary support.

kate: good call. let's document that in CHANGELOG and the exceptions section in the SDK reference.

jamal: will file PR tonight. assigning reviewers @arjun @tessa.

maria: thanks all. posting sample failing curl in case someone wants to reproduce: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/users -d '{"name":"A"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"` returns `HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity` and plain text body on my env.

tessa: :thumbsup:
